Hanging_Leg_Raise: Hang from a bar with your arms straight and your body still.
Raise your legs together (straight, or with bent knees, which is easier) to hip height or higher.
Lower with control without swinging. Try to curl your pelvis up slightly at the top.
Dead_Bug: Lie on your back with your arms reaching towards the ceiling and your knees bent at 90 degrees over your hips.
Press your lower back into the floor and at the same time lower one arm behind your head and the opposite leg towards the floor.
Return to the centre and repeat on the other side. Your back should not lift off the floor.
Crunches: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and hands on your chest or by your temples.
Lift your shoulders off the floor by curling your upper back, without pulling on your neck.
Squeeze your abs for a second and lower with control.
Russian_Twist: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and lean your torso back with a straight back.
With your hands together (or holding a weight), rotate your torso to bring them beside one hip.
Rotate to the other side and keep alternating. To make it harder, lift your feet off the floor.
Plank: Rest your forearms on the floor with your elbows under your shoulders and straighten your legs on your toes.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels, squeezing your abs and glutes.
Hold for the set time breathing normally, without letting your hips sag or rise.
Side_Bridge: Lie on your side resting on one forearm, elbow under your shoulder and legs straight, one on top of the other.
Lift your hips until your body is in a straight line.
Hold for the set time and switch sides.
Kettlebell_Windmill: Press a kettlebell overhead with a straight arm. Feet slightly wider than your shoulders, pointing away from the kettlebell.
Keeping your eyes on the kettlebell, push your hips towards the side of the arm holding it and slide your other hand down your leg towards the floor.
Come back up with the arm always vertical. Start light: it demands mobility and control.
Cable_Crunch: Kneel facing a high pulley with a rope, holding it beside your head.
Curl your torso, bringing your elbows towards your thighs, without moving your hips.
Squeeze your abs for a second and return with control.
Stomach_Vacuum: Standing, sitting or on all fours, breathe all the air out of your lungs.
Without breathing in again, draw your belly button in and up as far as you can.
Hold for a few seconds and relax. It works the transverse abdominis.
Mountain_Climbers: Get into a push-up position with your hands under your shoulders and your body straight.
Bring one knee towards your chest and extend it again while bringing in the other.
Alternate your legs at a good pace without letting your hips rise or sag.
Rope_Jumping: Hold the rope with your elbows close to your body and turn it with your wrists.
Jump with your feet together just high enough for the rope to pass, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Keep a steady pace for the set time.
Box_Jump_Multiple_Response: Stand in front of a stable box with your feet hip-width apart.
Bend your legs slightly, swing your arms and jump onto the box, landing on both feet at once with your knees bent.
Get down from the box (stepping down is better than jumping) and go straight into the next jump.
Choose a height you can jump safely.
Freehand_Jump_Squat: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and jump up explosively, using your arms.
Land softly by bending your legs and go straight into the next rep.
Battling_Ropes: Hold one end of the rope in each hand, legs slightly bent and torso leaning forward a little.
Move your arms up and down forcefully to make waves in the rope, alternating or together.
Keep the pace for the set time without rounding your back.
Bicycling: Adjust the saddle so your leg is almost straight with the pedal at the bottom.
Pedal at a pace you can sustain. Log the distance and time when you finish.
Wear a helmet and follow the traffic rules.
Bicycling_Stationary: Adjust the saddle so your leg is almost straight with the pedal at the bottom.
Pedal with the resistance and pace your training calls for.
Log the distance and time when you finish.
Elliptical_Trainer: Step onto the elliptical and hold the moving handles.
Move your legs and arms together at a steady pace with your torso upright.
Set the resistance for your training and log the distance and time when you finish.
Jogging_Treadmill: Step onto the treadmill and clip the safety key to your clothes.
Start walking and increase the speed to a gentle jog at which you can still talk.
Keep the pace for the set time and log the distance when you finish.
Running_Treadmill: Step onto the treadmill and clip the safety key to your clothes.
Warm up for a few minutes walking or jogging before moving up to your running pace.
Log the distance and time when you finish.
Trail_Running_Walking: Choose a route you know and take water, suitable footwear and your phone.
Walk or run at your own pace, shortening your stride uphill and taking care downhill.
Log the distance and time when you finish.
Walking_Treadmill: Step onto the treadmill and clip the safety key to your clothes.
Walk briskly with your back upright and your arms swinging. You can raise the incline to make it harder.
Log the distance and time when you finish.
Rowing_Stationary: Sit on the rower, strap your feet in and hold the handle with your arms straight.
Drive with your legs first, then lean your torso back slightly and finish by pulling the handle to your stomach.
Return in reverse order: arms, torso and legs. Log the distance and time when you finish.
Recumbent_Bike: Sit on the recumbent bike with your back supported and adjust the seat so your leg is almost straight.
Pedal with the resistance and pace your training calls for.
Log the distance and time when you finish.
Skating: Wear a helmet and pads and choose a suitable area.
Skate at a steady pace with your knees bent and your weight over the middle of your feet.
Log the distance and time when you finish.
Stairmaster: Step onto the machine and hold the handles without putting all your weight on them.
Climb the steps at a steady pace with your torso upright.
Keep the pace for the set time.
Step_Mill: Step onto the step mill and hold the handles without leaning your weight on them.
Climb the steps placing your whole foot, with your torso upright.
Keep the pace for the set time.
